<a id="adr-0059--crc32c-arm64-generato-da-common-lispsbcl"></a>

# ADR-0059 — ARM64 CRC32C generated by Common Lisp/SBCL

- **Status:** Accepted for the implementation authorized on 2026-10-23
- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **References:** REQ-FOR-003, REQ-AFF-002, REQ-AFF-004, INV-A3, INV-A4;
  [ADR-0001](0001-common-lisp-sbcl.md), [ADR-0034](0034-policy-di-compilazione-e-standard-di-codifica.md)

<a id="contesto-e-prova-discriminante"></a>

## Context and discriminating test

The [isolated benchmark](../implementazione/get-costi-risultati.md) measures about
5.8 microseconds per 4 KiB CRC. The preregistered
[SPK-08 CRC](../../spikes/SPK-08-generated-code/metodo-crc32c.md) spike compares
software and CRC32C instructions: 6,624 cases with a bitwise oracle, seeds, offsets, and
incrementality; five replicates per size. The 16 B block kernel
measures about 0.73 microseconds at 4 KiB, with zero observed heap allocation. The
64 B unrolled variant measures about 0.81 microseconds: it is not selected. Both
campaigns and the first assembler API error remain preserved.

<a id="decisione"></a>

## Decision

1. The `crc32c` API retains range, finalized seed/checksum, polynomial,
   errors, and persistent format. The slicing-by-8 algorithm remains available
   as fallback and differential reference; it is a required backend for
   platforms without qualified acceleration.
2. On SBCL 2.6.9, macOS ARM64, the I/O module queries `sysctlbyname`
   (`hw.optional.armv8_crc32`) before using the backend. Failure,
   absent feature, or unqualified system or version selects
   software. No probing by executing potentially illegal
   instructions; no external process in the product.
3. Two private VOPs implement CRC32CX and CRC32CB using only registers. Instruction
   encoding is emitted in Lisp through the SBCL
   assembler, with register constraints and opcode tests. The installed disassembler
   does not know these mnemonics and shows the four bytes.
4. The 16 B loads use SB-SIMD NEON APIs with bounds checks enabled at
   safety 3. No pointers/SAPs, pinning, unchecked array
   reinterpretation, or GC suspension in the checksum. The tail uses `aref` and CRC32CB.
   The Lisp vector retains its lifetime; no address survives
   an instruction or is retained between calls.
5. Kernel selection happens at load time, before starting readers
   or writers. A private function reference remains unchanged during
   service: GET does not query the OS/CPU or write shared state.
   Standalone loads of just the software file retain the fallback.
6. Spike code is not promoted. The C1 implementation has its own contracts,
   types, and checks. No change to commits, WAL, on-disk checksums,
   EBR, cache, or progress guarantees; no reduction in safety.

OS detection is part of the I/O module, though its small CPU
interface loads before the foundations, without circular dependencies.
Use of `sysctlbyname` follows the existing OS-binding pattern: all
repository code remains Common Lisp; no foreign checksum library.

<a id="verifica-e-limiti"></a>

## Verification and limits

Public/software/oracle differential checks, lengths and offsets at block
boundaries, every small split, arbitrary seeds, corruption, and invalid ranges;
standalone software, warning-free build, existing GET/record/WAL tests,
allocations, FASL compilation, and two C1 readings. Overall verification
must pass before delivery. Byte-by-byte oracle checking
remains in the integrity suite; a separate throughput campaign
moves it outside timing and checks the result after every window.

0.4–0.6 microseconds per CRC and 2 microseconds per GET remain targets;
obtained numbers are published without subtraction from the historical benchmark.
Linux/x86-64 and Linux/ARM64 retain software; acceleration on other
platforms requires its own detection and qualification. Different SBCL versions
do not enable the kernel without new qualification.

Primary sources: [Arm CRC32C](https://support.arm.com/documentation/100069/0609/A64-General-Instructions/CRC32CB--CRC32CH--CRC32CW--CRC32CX?lang=en),
[SBCL ARM64](https://github.com/sbcl/sbcl/tree/master/src/compiler/arm64).
